title: Welcome
body: The header has the light/dark switch and ⚙ for detector settings. The yellow banner is always there: SWALLOHear is a research prototype, not a diagnostic device.

title: Pick a recording
body: Four sources: demo clips from held-out test participants, upload, the phone microphone, or synthetic test signals. Here: demo clip ns027d_1.

title: Verdict and summary
body: First the quality gate, then the verdict: events detected. The cards show confident and low-confidence events, event rate, estimated SNR against the gate, and processing time.

title: Timeline
body: Waveform, spectrogram and detector score on one time axis. Teal = Confident, amber = Low-confidence, dotted green = expert labels. Zoom up to 8× and swipe sideways.

title: Event card
body: Tap a numbered marker to inspect an event: listen to just that sound, see its reliability against the threshold and what raised or lowered it, then record your own call.

title: Events and “Why this score?”
body: A table of every event, then an exact breakdown of the reliability score: it starts from an average event and each measurement pushes it up (teal) or down (amber).

title: Rhythm
body: How swallowing is spread over time: rate, mean interval, regularity and the longest pause, with events-over-time and interval charts. Shown here on clip s007a_2, which has six events.

title: Robustness lab
body: Re-runs the analysis at seven noise levels. Watch the events thin out and the quality gate start withholding results once the estimated SNR falls below the red line.

title: Signal quality
body: Every quality-gate check with its value and limit, how the SNR is estimated (noise floor vs peaks) and the average spectrum, where mains hum would show as spikes.

title: Expert comparison
body: For labelled clips: matched events, false detections, misses, precision, recall and F1, and Expert vs System lanes (green = matched, red = unmatched).

title: Session log
body: Every analysis run in this session, with exports of the log and of all your calls on events.

title: Stress test
body: Add white, pink or 60 Hz mains-hum noise, or simulate clipping. At 10 dB of white noise the estimated SNR drops below the gate and the result is withheld instead of guessed.

title: Detector settings
body: All five thresholds, live. Raising the reliability threshold makes fewer events Confident but more of them correct. “Reset to validated” restores the values the results were measured with.

title: Printable report
body: 📄 Report opens a self-contained report in the browser: verdict, timeline, every event with its reasons and your calls, rhythm, quality and limits, ready to share or save as PDF.

title: Upload a file
body: Choose any audio file on the phone (WAV, FLAC, M4A, MP3, WebM; up to 120 s). It is sent to the analysis server and analysed exactly like the demo clips.

title: Record with the microphone
body: Rest the phone’s microphone lightly against the side of the throat and press record. When you stop, the recording is analysed straight away. (Here a test tone stands in for a throat recording.)

title: Synthetic test signals
body: Generated swallow-like bursts with known positions, for checking the pipeline end to end. Sliders set the number of bursts, the length and the random seed.

title: Compare
body: Two recordings side by side, here the same clip clean and with 5 dB of noise: a table with a B − A column, both detector scores overlaid, and timelines on a shared time axis.

title: Batch
body: Analyse many recordings at once, with optional noise: totals, a table with mean reliability and F1, and an SNR-vs-events chart against the quality gate.

title: Method & results
body: How the pipeline works and what the experiments showed: noise robustness, and ordinary vs reliability-aware output at each noise level, then the headline numbers and limits.

title: Dark mode
body: ☾ switches the whole app, charts included, and the choice stays as you move between tabs.
